earlier_scan.source_named: Glottolog kara1475 lists zero references; language marked Unattested, ISO xkh retired as duplicate of Waiwai.

sources.citation: ISO 639-3 Registration Authority. 2015. Change Request Number 2015-038: retire [xkh] Karahawyana (adopted 2016-01-15). SIL International.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Rationale (p.2): Karahawyana is equivalent to [waw] Waiwai; 'Hammarstrom (2015) cites several sources as evidence that Karahawyana is a dialect of Waiwai (Frikel 1957:59, Frikel 1958:141, FUNAI 1984:59, Howard 2001)'. No linguistic data of any kind.

sources.citation: Acacio, M. J. C. 2011. Fonologia da lingua Waiwai (MA thesis, UFPA) [held for waiw1244].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Checked only for Karahawyana content: mentions 'karapayana' once (p.31 area, quoting the PIB ethnographic summary) as one of the other Karib languages spoken in Waiwai villages; gives no data on that variety. Its Waiwai stress statement belongs to waiw1244, already catalogued.

sources.citation: Hawkins, W. Neill. 1962. A morfologia do substantivo na lingua uaiuai. Museu Nacional, Publicacoes Avulsas 21 [held for waiw1244].
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.harvard_location: Tozzer Library (offsite storage), call number MUS.19.5.2 (21)
sources.note: a full-text search for stress/accent text layer: no mention of Karahawyana/Karafawyana/Karapawyana; its Waiwai stress note (sect. 2.1) belongs to waiw1244.

sources.citation: Frikel, Protasio. 1958. Classificacao linguistico-etnologica das tribos indigenas do Para Setentrional e zonas adjacentes. Revista de Antropologia (Sao Paulo) 6(2): 113-188 (p.141).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Cited in the ISO retirement rationale for the Karahawyana = Waiwai-dialect identification; Revista de Antropologia back issues are open at revistas.usp.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Category 'Unattested'; most extensive description = Frikel 1957, graded 'a wordlist or less'; zero grammar/phonology/sketch references.

sources.citation: Instituto Socioambiental, Povos Indigenas no Brasil: 'Waiwai' (Evelyn Schuler Zea).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Nothing. Names Karapawyana/Karapayana among kindreds 'falando outras linguas Karib' who lived in Waiwai villages 1950-80 and are now refounding villages where their own language dominates; ethnographic only.

sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Lists Karafawyana as a Waiwai dialect; phonology section (from Hawkins 1998) gives segment inventory only, no stress statement, nothing specific to Karafawyana.

sources.citation: Hammarstrom, Harald. 2015. Ethnologue 16/17/18th editions: A comprehensive review: Online appendices. Language 91(3): s1-s188 (entry for [xkh]).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained

sources.note: Compiles the evidence that Karahawyana is a Waiwai dialect; would settle the identity note, not the stress rule.

sources.citation: Howard, Catherine V. 2001. Wrought Identities: The Waiwai expeditions in search of the unseen 'tribes' of Northern Amazonia. PhD dissertation, University of Chicago (ch. 'Pacifying the fierce peoples', pp. 284-314).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Ethnography of the 1974-80 contact expeditions to the Jatapu Karapawyana; may state what the Karapawyana spoke at contact and how close it was to Waiwai. No phonology expected.

sources.citation: Frikel, Protasio. 1957. Zur linguistisch-ethnologischen Gliederung der Indianerstamme von Nord-Para (Brasilien) und den anliegenden Gebieten. Anthropos 52: 509-563 (p.59 of offprint cited for Karahawyana).

sources.note: Glottolog's only (Glottolog's most extensive description) reference for kara1475; would confirm whether any Karahawyana word forms were ever recorded (graded 'a wordlist or less'). Unlikely to contain a stress statement but is the sole primary mention.
